title: Impact of ACA Individual Mandate on Insurance Premiums

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with unit and time fixed effects, tailored for staggered enforcement. I complement the baseline two-way FE DID with (i) a modern staggered-DID estimator (Callaway & Sant’Anna, 2021) that aggregates group-time ATTs and (ii) an event-study (Sun & Abraham, 2020 via sunab) to assess dynamics and pre-trends.
- Why: The ACA individual mandate was enforced at different times across regions, so staggered adoption methods avoid bias from heterogeneous and dynamic treatment effects that can affect traditional TWFE.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of enforcement, treated and not-yet-treated (or never-treated) regions would follow similar premium trends.
  - No anticipation: Regions’ premiums do not adjust in advance of their own enforcement date.
  - Stable composition and SUTVA: No compositional changes confounding the treatment and no spillovers across regions.
  - For the Callaway & Sant’Anna estimator: Appropriate control group (not-yet-treated) is valid at each time.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Packages
pkgs <- c("fixest", "did", "data.table")
for (p in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p)
}
library(fixest)
library(did)
library(data.table)

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s41_data.csv"
dt <- fread(path)

# Ensure proper types
dt[, unit_id := as.integer(unit_id)]
dt[, period := as.integer(period)]
dt[, treated := as.integer(treated)]
dt[, post := as.integer(post)]
dt[, treat_x_post := as.integer(treat_x_post)]
dt[, y := as.numeric(y)]

# 2) Construct first enforcement (cohort) g for each unit
# g = first period when treat_x_post == 1; g = 0 for never-treated
dt[, g := {
  idx <- which(treat_x_post == 1)
  if (length(idx) == 0) 0L else min(period[idx])
}, by = unit_id]

# Basic sample diagnostics
cat("Sample size:", nrow(dt), "\n")
cat("Unique units:", length(unique(dt$unit_id)), "\n")
cat("Unique periods:", length(unique(dt$period)), "\n")
cat("Treated units (ever):", length(unique(dt$unit_id[dt$g > 0])), "\n")
cat("Never-treated units:", length(unique(dt$unit_id[dt$g == 0])), "\n\n")

# 3) Baseline TWFE DID: y_it = alpha_i + lambda_t + beta * 1{treated & post_it} + e_it
# Cluster SE by unit_id
m_twfe <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id)

beta <- coef(m_twfe)[["treat_x_post"]]
se_beta <- sqrt(diag(vcov(m_twfe)))[["treat_x_post"]]
ci_lo <- beta - 1.96 * se_beta
ci_hi <- beta + 1.96 * se_beta

pct <- 100 * (exp(beta) - 1)
pct_lo <- 100 * (exp(ci_lo) - 1)
pct_hi <- 100 * (exp(ci_hi) - 1)

cat("Baseline TWFE DID (clustered by unit):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Log-point effect (beta): %.4f (SE = %.4f), 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n", beta, se_beta, ci_lo, ci_hi))
cat(sprintf("  Implied %% change in premiums: %.2f%%, 95%% CI [%.2f%%, %.2f%%]\n\n", pct, pct_lo, pct_hi))

# 4) Robustness A: Two-way clustered SE (unit and period)
m_twfe_twoc <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id + period)
beta2 <- coef(m_twfe_twoc)[["treat_x_post"]]
se_beta2 <- sqrt(diag(vcov(m_twfe_twoc)))[["treat_x_post"]]
ci_lo2 <- beta2 - 1.96 * se_beta2
ci_hi2 <- beta2 + 1.96 * se_beta2
pct2 <- 100 * (exp(beta2) - 1)
pct_lo2 <- 100 * (exp(ci_lo2) - 1)
pct_hi2 <- 100 * (exp(ci_hi2) - 1)

cat("TWFE DID with two-way clustered SE (unit, period):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Log-point effect (beta): %.4f (SE = %.4f), 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n", beta2, se_beta2, ci_lo2, ci_hi2))
cat(sprintf("  Implied %% change in premiums: %.2f%%, 95%% CI [%.2f%%, %.2f%%]\n\n", pct2, pct_lo2, pct_hi2))

# 5) Robustness B: Event-study (Sun & Abraham via sunab) to assess dynamics and pre-trends
# Use period - g relative time implicitly through sunab; set -1 as reference
m_es <- feols(y ~ sunab(g, period, ref.p = -1) | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id)

cat("Event-study (Sun & Abraham) estimated event-time coefficients (subset):\n")
ct <- coeftable(m_es)
# Keep only sunab terms
sunab_rows <- grep("^sunab\\(", rownames(ct))
ct_sunab <- ct[sunab_rows, , drop = FALSE]

# Extract event-time from the row names for sorting/printing
# Row names usually contain 'sunab(g, period)::event_k'
extract_event <- function(x) {
  # Try to parse the trailing event time integer from the name
  # Works for patterns like 'sunab(g, period)::k'
  parts <- strsplit(x, "::")[[1]]
  as.integer(gsub("[^\\-0-9]", "", parts[length(parts)]))
}
ev <- sapply(rownames(ct_sunab), extract_event)
ord <- order(ev)
ct_sunab <- ct_sunab[ord, , drop = FALSE]
ev_sorted <- ev[ord]

# Print a compact subset: a few leads and lags if available
to_print_idx <- which(ev_sorted %in% c(-3, -2, 0, 1, 2, 3))
if (length(to_print_idx) == 0) {
  to_print_idx <- seq_len(min(8, nrow(ct_sunab)))
}
for (i in to_print_idx) {
  est <- ct_sunab[i, 1]
  se  <- ct_sunab[i, 2]
  evi <- ev_sorted[i]
  cat(sprintf("  Event time %d: coef = %.4f (SE = %.4f)\n", evi, est, se))
}
cat("\n")

# 6) Robustness C: Callaway & Sant’Anna (2021) staggered DID, overall ATT and dynamics
# Use not-yet-treated as controls; cluster by unit; panel data
out_cs <- att_gt(yname = "y",
                 tname = "period",
                 idname = "unit_id",
                 gname = "g",
                 data = as.data.frame(dt),
                 control_group = "notyet",
                 panel = TRUE,
                 clustervars = "unit_id")

agg_overall <- aggte(out_cs, type = "overall")
att <- agg_overall$overall.att
se_att <- agg_overall$overall.se
ci_lo_att <- att - 1.96 * se_att
ci_hi_att <- att + 1.96 * se_att
pct_att <- 100 * (exp(att) - 1)
pct_lo_att <- 100 * (exp(ci_lo_att) - 1)
pct_hi_att <- 100 * (exp(ci_hi_att) - 1)

cat("Callaway & Sant’Anna overall ATT:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Log-point ATT: %.4f (SE = %.4f), 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n", att, se_att, ci_lo_att, ci_hi_att))
cat(sprintf("  Implied %% change in premiums: %.2f%%, 95%% CI [%.2f%%, %.2f%%]\n\n", pct_att, pct_lo_att, pct_hi_att))

# Dynamics from Callaway & Sant’Anna (event time relative to g)
agg_dyn <- aggte(out_cs, type = "dynamic")
cat("Callaway & Sant’Anna dynamic effects (subset of event times):\n")
# Print few leads and lags if available
dyn_df <- data.frame(event_time = agg_dyn$egt, att = agg_dyn$att.egt, se = agg_dyn$se.egt)
subset_dyn <- dyn_df[dyn_df$event_time %in% c(-3, -2, 0, 1, 2, 3), ]
if (nrow(subset_dyn) == 0) {
  subset_dyn <- head(dyn_df[order(dyn_df$event_time), ], 8)
}
apply(subset_dyn, 1, function(r) {
  cat(sprintf("  Event time %d: ATT = %.4f (SE = %.4f)\n",
              as.integer(r["event_time"]), as.numeric(r["att"]), as.numeric(r["se"])))
})
cat("\n")

# 7) Placebo check: Shift treatment timing forward by 2 periods for treated units
max_t <- max(dt$period)
dt[, g_placebo := ifelse(g > 0, pmin(g + 2L, max_t + 100L), 0L)]  # shift beyond sample if needed
out_placebo <- att_gt(yname = "y",
                      tname = "period",
                      idname = "unit_id",
                      gname = "g_placebo",
                      data = as.data.frame(dt),
                      control_group = "notyet",
                      panel = TRUE,
                      clustervars = "unit_id")

agg_placebo <- aggte(out_placebo, type = "overall")
cat("Placebo overall ATT (shift g by +2 periods):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Log-point ATT: %.4f (SE = %.4f)\n\n", agg_placebo$overall.att, agg_placebo$overall.se))

# 8) Final printed headline result (baseline TWFE)
cat("Headline result: Baseline TWFE DID implies a", sprintf("%.2f", pct), "% change in premiums.\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. The individual mandate should broaden the risk pool by bringing in healthier enrollees, lowering average expected costs and thus premiums.
- Magnitude: A modest decline, roughly 2–5 percent in log premiums. In log points, about −0.02 to −0.05. Effects may build over a few periods post-enforcement; pre-trends should be near zero if identification is valid.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare regions before and after mandate enforcement.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The enforcement of the mandate led to a decrease in insurance premiums.
